scope.purpose: Trigger an action or move to the next step of a task with a short visible label.
useCases: Primary, secondary and tertiary actions in forms, dialogs, toolbars and page headers (intent x appearance hierarchy).
Asynchronous actions with a loading state that keeps the width and focus.
A task-oriented navigation that looks like an action (href, e.g. Create project).
Optional leading icon; optional trailing icon, counter or keyboard shortcut.
exclusions: Toggle buttons with a pressed state (aria-pressed): SegmentedControl or a future ToggleButton.
Split buttons and menu triggers with an integrated chevron (Menu, wave 3).
Button groups and toolbars: composition patterns.
Full-width stretching as a prop: layout decides the width (open decision 1).
alternatives: IconButton for an action without visible text.
Menu for a list of actions behind one trigger.

fixtures: Local inline SVG icons (Phosphor paths) in examples and tests, standing in for Icon.
Local counter and shortcut fixtures in examples and tests, standing in for Counter and Shortcut.

checks.note: Schema, consistency and token coverage (131 paths) in 18 contexts.
6264 checks, 0 failures on the contrastScope backdrops (canvas, default, subtle, muted, raised, overlay) in 18 contexts; outline border on muted in dark is informational (contract gate decision).

Rebuilt as a single bundle and smoke-checked from file:// in Chromium. The first published preview (artifact version 1) was blank: it referenced a chunk shared with the foundations page that was not inlined.

decisionsTaken: No token additions: every role reuses the approved semantic inventory (color.action.*, size.control.*, space.control.*, typography.label.*, size.icon.*, focus.*, motion.*).
Icon size follows the button size (sm 16, md 20, lg 24 px) through size.icon.{size}.
href turns the button into a link with identical appearance, because the catalog allows Button to navigate to a task; disabled or loading never navigates.
Loading keeps the button focusable and busy (label kept as accessible name); disabled removes it from focus.
Label is a required plain string (one line, truncated visually) rather than free content, to guarantee an accessible name.
Form submission type (submit/reset) is an implementation mechanic passed through to the native element, not a contract option.
Documented backdrops for Button: canvas, default, subtle, raised, overlay and muted; inverse and scrim are not supported backdrops.
No width option: layout stretches the button (open decision 1, accepted at the contract gate).
Outline border contrast on surface.muted in dark appearances accepted (open decision 2, accepted at the contract gate): the label identifies the button.
Contract event activate is exposed as the onactivate callback prop; a native onclick passed through is guarded the same way.
type defaults to button so that a Button never submits a form by accident; submit and reset are passed through.
Leading and trailing content is hidden from assistive technology: the label is the whole accessible name.
Loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled but not the native disabled attribute, so focus stays on the button.

The root element is the 44 px interaction target (block size) and a centered pseudo-element extends it to 44 px wide; the visible container fills the root, so a layout that stretches the button stretches its surface.
The loading indicator is an inline SVG spinner in the content color (800 ms turn, slowed to 2.4 s under reduced motion).
Contrast is checked on the backdrops declared in status contrastScope (a generic tooling addition, documented in authoring/architecture.md).
Typography roles now also bind letterSpacing and fontFeatureSettings helpers in generated component CSS (generic build-svelte addition).

Spacing variant F chosen by the user at the implementation review (2026-09-27): side spacing split in thirds, two parts edge padding, one part label margin, on existing primitives. Comparison page examples/button-spacing (commit cf0c477, artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/7PPpXnsQav9VsAuv4FR7DW v2), removed after the choice.

New semantic roles space.control.edge-inline.{sm,md,lg} and space.control.label-inline.{sm,md,lg} (density axis) rather than changing padding-inline and gap, which other controls (fields) will keep using. Values: compact 4+2, 8+4, 12+6; standard 8+4, 12+6, 16+8; comfortable 12+6, 16+8, 20+10.
Semantic roles kept for the spacing (option 1, user 2026-09-27): values vary by density, which component tokens cannot do in the current architecture.

Optical spacing (2026-09-27, after the user noticed leading icons looked farther from the label than trailing counters and shortcuts): icons are placed by their drawing. Phosphor icons draw 1/8 of their box inside on each side, so icon boxes overlap edgeInline and labelInline by iconSize/8. Measured visible gaps in md: edge to icon 12.5, icon to label 6.5, label to counter 7.25, counter to edge 13 (before: 15.25, 10.25, 6.25, 12).
Review fixtures now use real Phosphor 2.1.1 regular icons (MIT) instead of hand-drawn stroke icons, so the review shows the reference geometry.
openDecisions: Visual balance (implementation review 2026-09-27): tune per size in examples/button-balance (artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/2 pending) the edge padding and label margin (proposal: lg label 8 -> 10), vertical centering on capital letters (text-box trim, measured 0 px offset in all sizes versus up to 0.5 px too high without), and tight ellipsis (label box fitted to the visible text by script; native CSS leaves 1.4 to 13.4 px after the ellipsis). The chosen settings change contract spacing facts and possibly token values; values for compact and comfortable follow once standard is chosen.
aria-disabled while loading (in addition to aria-busy): keep or expose only the busy state.
nextAction: Contract gate for the spacing fact and token additions, then implementation gate on the updated preview (artifact version 3).
implementationNotes: Bits UI Button.Root owns the button/link element switch and the disabled link semantics (no href, aria-disabled, tabindex -1).
Loading is guarded in the click handler; Enter and Space on a native button and Enter on a link dispatch click, so one guard covers pointer and keyboard.
The horizontal target pseudo-element uses physical left + translateX(-50%) on purpose: centering is symmetric in both writing directions.

informational.reason: Accepted at the contract gate (2026-09-26): outline border reaches 2.06 to 2.37 on surface.muted in dark; the label identifies the button, WCAG 1.4.11 does not require the boundary.
